Mr. Abdul Quiyum, Senior Advocate (with Mr. Ali Reza, Advocate) instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record, For the Appellant. 
Mr. M.I. Farooqui, Senior Advocate (with Ms. Nazneen Nahar, Advocate) instructed by Ms. Mahmuda Begum, Advocate-on-Record, For Respondent No. 1.

full_judgment:
5. The defendant-appellants contested the suits by filing written statements. Their case, in short, was that the suit property of No.1 Atash Khana Lane, along with other property owned by Khiroda Shundari Daishya. Khiroda sold the entire suit property to Salimunnesa by a registered kabala dated 27/03/1953 and delivered possession. Salimunnesa transferred her 8(eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and the rest 8(eight) annas to Mohammad Ilias on 15/06/1959, Ilias, by a registered deed of gift, transferred his said 8 (eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and delivered possession. Thus, Rasheda Begum became 16 (sixteen) annas owner and possessor of the suit property. One Munjurul Hoq was tenant in a portion of the suit property. He defaulted to pay rent. Accordingly, Rasheda filed Money Suit No.50 of 1959 in the 3rd Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka for the realization of arrear rent. Rasheda Begum also filed House Rent Case No.598 of 1959 for eviction of Dr. Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed. The tenant, forging signatures of Rasheda Begum, filed two applications for compromise in the name of Rasheda Begum and Khatimunnesa respectively in the said money suit and House Rent case and obtained compromise decrees. Knowing about the same, Rasheda Begum filed Title Suit No.221 of 1964 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka praying for cancellation of the deeds of agreement dated 16/11/1959 as well compromise petitions filed in Money Suit No.50 of 1959 and House Rent Case No.598 of 1959 and for setting aside those fraudulent compromise decrees. In which, Khatimunnesa and Dr. Manjurul Haque appeared and filed written statement claiming that they had purchased 7(seven) annas share of the suit holding in auction on 20.06.1953. Title Suit No.221 of 1964 was decreed on 25.12.1965 in favour of Rasheda Begum. Against that judgment and decree, Dr. Manjurul Haque and his wife Khatimunnesa preferred Title Appeal No.50 of 1966 which was dismissed on 19.07.1966. Dr. Manjurul Haque and his wife preferred Second Appeal No.1095 of 1966 in the then High Court and said Second Appeal was also dismissed. Thus, the right, title and possession of Rasheda Begum in the suit property was confirmed. While in possession of the suit property, Rasheda Begum entered into a contract with the defendants to sell the same at a consideration of Tk.45,000/-, and, on receipt of a sum of Tk. 15,000/-, as advance she executed a "bainapatra" on 12.08.1972. Since Rasheda Begum was avoiding execution and registration of the kabala deed, the defendants filed Title Suit No.62 of 1979 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract. The suit was decreed on 15.11.1979 and the defendants got the kabala deed executed and registered on 27.02.1980 through Court in Title Execution Case No.03 of 1980. After registration of the kabala deed, when the defendants went to take over possession of the suit property through Court, the plaintiffs resisted the bailiff of the Court and the bailiff returned the 'writ of delivery' without executing the same with the prayer for police help. Meanwhile, the plaintiff's filed Title Suit No.329 of 1980 in the third Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka for permanent injunction and obtained decree, which was set aside by the Appellate Court on 24.01.1987 in Title Appeal No. 1969 of 1984 preferred by the defendants. The decree of the Appellate Court was upheld in Civil Revision No.76 of 1987 by the High Court Division as well as in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.297 of 1992 by the Appellate Division. Thereafter, the defendants prayed for police help to execute the decree and the Court allowed the prayer. The plaintiffs filed an application under Order XXI, Rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure just to obstruct the further proceedings of title Execution Case No.3 of 1980. The application was rejected on 23.01.1994 on contest. Thereafter, the plaintiffs filed the instant suit making false and frivolous allegations just to continue with their unauthorized possession in, the suit property depriving the defendants of the enjoyment of the fruits of the aforesaid decree. They denied that they had dispossessed the plaintiffs by force from the suit property on 16.09.1997 and also denied the story of looting away the goods from the suit property. When Title Execution Case No.3 of 1980 was revived, the plaintiffs filed an application for staying further proceedings of the same but their prayer was rejected on 29.01.1994. Against the said order, the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No.465 of 1994 in the High Court Division and obtained rule which was discharged on 27.08.1997 with a direction upon them to hand over possession of the suit property to the defendants within 30(thirty) days. After getting possession of the suit land, the defendants demolished the kancha and semi pucca rooms standing thereon. They completed major portion of works for construction of a multistoried building investing huge amount. Remaining work is also under process. 

 7. These appellants contested the said Money Suit by tiling written statement denying the claim. 

 10. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, with Mr. Ali Reza, learned Counsel appearing for the appellants, submits, that as per gazette notification dated 2nd April 1956 vide Memo Nos.4024 LR and LR 4836 under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the rent receiving interest of the landlords of Dhaka District was vested in the Government and that the exhibit-1 shows that Khiroda Sundari held a "Merash Ijara" interest under the private landlord which conclusively proved that the papers of Certificate Case No.660 of 1952-53 issued by R.L. Government Acquired Estate (exhibits-2 and 2Ka) are forged and manufactured documents. He further submits that the Certificate Case No.660 of 1952-53 was allegedly filed by the Government for arrear of rent but the exhibits-2 and 2(Ka) show that certificate case was filed by R.L. Government Acquired Estate which was contrary to the provisions of the Public Demand Recovery Act and there is nothing in the evidence on record that while holding auction the provisions of the PDR Act had been complied with. He further submits that Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Mazharul Haque, forging ext.2 and 2(Ka), claimed his title in the suit property but earlier such claim had not been accepted by the Courts in different cases, the Courts below ignoring the earlier observation of the Courts, erroneously decreed the suit. He further submits that after long lapse of time of making adverse observation by the competent Court as to title of the plaintiffs, they filed this suit which was hopelessly barred by limitation. He further submits that the plaintiffs prayed for decree in the entire land of the disputed plot inasmuch as their predecessor Ali Ahmed allegedly auction purchased only 7 annas share of the disputed holding and plot, in such view of the matter, without specification of their 7 annas share of the alleged auction purchased land or prayer for partition, the suit was not maintainable, the Courts below erred in law in not dismissing the suit. 

 11. Mr. M.I. Farooqui, learned Senior Counsel appearing with Ms. Nazneen Nahar for the respondents, submits that all the courts below finding the sale certificate (Ext-2) and writ of delivery of possession (Ext-2-Ka) genuine decreed the suit. This Division, in review petition, is not authorized to reverse the finding of fact as to the nature of the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession. He submits that the Certificate case was started by R.L. Government Acquired Estate due to non-payment of rent against the C.S. recorded tenants, namely, Khiroda Sundari and Lalit Mohon Shaha and certificate holder put the disputed property in auction and predecessor-in-interest of the present respondents auction purchased the same on 20th June 1953 and got delivery of possession of the same through Court and the certificate purchaser took over possession of the same on 05.01.1954 (vide exhibit-2Ka) and the Courts of facts below finding the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession genuine decreed the suit, this Division rightly dismissed the civil petition. He lastly submits that the rent receiving interest of the landlord in respect of the suit land was acquired on 28.02.1952 under section 3(1) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act followed by extraordinary Gazette Notification dated Friday 12, 1954 bearing No.1815 L.R. 6th February 1954, by which, the compensation Assessment was prepared in respect of Ruplal Wards Estate under section 46A(1) of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act , in such view of the matter, there is no error of law apparent on the face of the record in the order of this Division. 

 16. The plaintiffs' case was that the suit land was put in auction in Certificate Case No.660 of 1952-53. Ali Ahmed auction purchased the same on 20th June 1953 which was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and said Ali Ahmed got sale certificate on 19.11.1953 and took over possession of the same on 20.01.1954. It appears from Sale Certificate (Exhibit-2) that certificate holder was R.L. Government Acquired Estate and certificate debtors were Khiroda Sundori and Lalit Mohon Saha. Ext.1 C.S. Khatian shows that Khiroda was the only tenant of the holding but in the Sale Certificate name of Lalit Mohan Saha appeared with her which clearly indicated that arrear was chargeable against Lalit Mohan as well. It is not understandable as to why, for charge of Lalit Mohan, requisition was given for holding auction of the property of Khiroda. From the schedule of property as described in sale certificate it appears that in the column of the name of the certificate holder R.L. Government Acquired Estate was mentioned and at second page of the same it appears the Certificate Officer was of the office of Das Group Govt.—AD Estate who put his signature in the Sale Certificate on 19.1 1.1957. We did not find any explanation neither in the plaint nor in the evidence nor from the learned Counsel of the plaintiff-respondents as to why sale certificate of R.L. Government Acquired Estate was issued by the Certificate Officer of 'Das Group Govt.-Ad Estate' on 19.11.1957. There is nothing in the pleading or in evidence as to how and when the rent receiving interest of landlord Laxminarayan was devolved upon to R.L. Govt. AD Estate since C.S. Khatian shows that Laxminarayan was the landlord. Section 4 of the Public Demand and Recovery Act (PDR Act)prescribes the mode of filing of certificate for Public demand payable to the Collector and directs that when the certificate officer is satisfied that any public demand payable to the Collector is due, he may sign a certificate in the prescribed form stating that the demand is due. Section 5 provides that when any public demand payable to any person other than the Collector is due such person may send written requisition in the prescribed form to the certificate officer. Section 6 of the PDR Act provides that on receipt of such requisition the certificate officer, if lie is satisfied that the demand is recoverable and that recovery is not barred by law, may sign a certificate in the prescribed form stating that the demand is due. Section 7 provides that when a certificate has been filed in the office of the certificate officer under section 4 or 6, he shall cause to be served upon the certificate debtor in the prescribed manner a notice in the prescribed form and a copy of the certificate. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that certificate holder R.L. Govt. Acquired Estate had any demand (Public demand?) chargeable from the certificate debtors Khiroda Sundari Saha and Lalit Mohan Saha(?) for which, it made requisition to the Certificate Officer of 'Das Group Govt.-Ad Estate' who issued notice in Form 2 of schedule II and being satisfied that the demand was chargeable or became due so he signed the certificate. 

 17. 'Public demand' means any arrear or money mentioned or referred to in schedule-1, i and includes any interest which may, by law, be chargeable thereon up to the date on which a certificate is signed under part II of the PDR Act. It is to be mentioned here that as per provision Section 3(3) of the PDR Act "Certificate Officer" means a collector and any officer, appointed by a Collector to perform the functions of a Certificate Officer under the Act. The Court of Wards can send requisition under section 5 of the PDR Act but requirement is that on receipt of a requisition filed under section 5 the Certificate Officer before signing a certificate must be satisfied, far as the demand made in the requisition is concerned, that it is recoverable. There is no evidence that Deputy Collector appointed any one/officer of Das Group Govt. AD Estate as Certificate Officer. 

 18. From Ext.1 C.S. Khatian No.241 of Mouza Shahar Dhaka it appears that Landlord of the suit holding was Laxminarayan and tenant was Khairoda Sundari Dashya of No.1 Atosh Khan Lane. Mr. M. I. Faruqui in her written submission stated that R.L (Rup Lal) Estate was owner of 7 annas share of Dhaka Collectorate Touzi No.61/1 and Wards Estate being managed by the Government under the Court of Wards Act. R.L.(Rup Lal) Estate, as a Wards Estate, was ultimately acquired by the Government under sections 3(i)(ii) and 4 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act vide Gazette Notification No.2906 L.R. dated 28.02.1952 as appeared in Gazette Notification No.1815 L.R. dated 6th February 1954. Accordingly, he drew our attention to the Dacca Gazette Extra ordinary dated February 12, 1954. He further stated, in his written submission, that after acquiring the rent receiving interest, in order to realise the arrear rent from the defaulted tenant of C.S. holding No.241 of Plot No.390/3940 Khiroda Sundari Dasya of the said Touzi No.61/1, R.L. Government Acquired Estate filed certificate Case No.660 of 1952-53 under section 62 read with sections 139 and 141 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and put in auction of Khiroda Sundari Dashya's said holding measuring .0568 acre on 20.06.1953 and predecessor of the plaintiffs Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Manjurul Haque purchased the said holding in auction. We are unable to accept the submission of Mr. Faruqui for the reasons that there is nothing in the pleadings or in evidence as to how and when the rent receiving interest of Landlord Laxminarayon was devolved upon R.L. Govt. Acquired Estate. Rent receiving interest of all the rent receivers were acquired with effect from 14th April 1956 under section 3 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as amended by East Bengal Ordinance Ill of 1956 in the district of Dhaka vide Notification Nos.4826 L.R. to 4836 LR, respectively, published in Dacca Gazette Extraordinary dated 2nd April 1956, part. From No.4836 LR of the Dacca Gazette dated April 2nd 1956 it appears that Governor acquired, with effect from the 14th April 1956, all interests of all rent-receivers in their respective estates, teluks, tenants, holdings and tenancies situated in the District of Dhaka, including their interests in all sub-soil except the interests and rights which have already been acquired by, and have already vested in, the Provincial Government under the Provisions of the said Act. Mr. Faruqui, drawing our attention to serial No.103 of the Dacca Gazette dated 12.02.1954, submits that the suit land was acquired vide 2906 LR dated 28.02.1952. But serial No.103 shows that names of the ex-rent receivers are Babu Jogesh Chandra Das son of Radhaballav Das, Babu Tarak Nath Das son Romesh Chandra Das, of Farashgonj, Dacca (Wards, Ruplal Wards Estate, Dacca). We do not find anywhere in the pleadings or in evidence as to how and when the rent receiving interest of the disputed holding was devolved upon to Babu Jogesh Chandra Das and others. In such view of the matter, it is difficult to accept that the suit property fell within the purview of exception mentioned in notification No.4836 LR. There is no reason to accept that Ruplal Wards Estate, Dacca and R.L Govt. Acquired Estate are same estate and landlords are same in absence of any pleadings and evidence with that regard. Serial No.103 shows that Babu Jogesh Chandra Das and Babu Tarak Nath Das are of Farashganj but C.S. Khatian shows that the suit land is situated within Mouza Shahar Dhaka under Kotwali Police Station. From C.S. Khatian No.241 it appears that land of holding No.241 is situated under Kotwali Police Station. But Sale Certificate (ext.2) shows that the same is situated under Lalbag Police Station. In C.S. Khatian; Touzi number was mentioned as No.61 but in Sale Certificate Touzi No. was shown as 61/1. In C.S. Khatian, name of the Mouza appeared as Shahar Dhaka but in Sale Certificate Mouza was shown as Atosh Khana. The plaintiffs did not take any step to connect each other. 

 20. Another aspect is that it is well settled that the certificate of sale does not, by itself, create the title but is merely evidence of title. In the case of Ahmedabad Municipality Vs. Hazi Abdul reported in AIR 1971 SC 1201 it was observed by the Supreme Court of India that it is axiomatic that the purchaser at auction sale takes the property subject to all the defects of title and the doctrine caveat emptor (let the purchaser beware) applies to such purchaser. It is the "right, title and interest" of the judgment-debtor with all risk and defect and without any warranty of title either by the decree-holder or by the court that passes to a purchaser at a court sale, with the exception that where it is proved that the judgment-debtor had no saleable interest at all the purchaser may recover back the purchase-money. In this case, the alleged auction was held on 20.06.1953 showing Khiroda Sundari Saha and Lalit Mohon Saha as certificate debtors. But we have already found from C.S. Khatian (ext-1) shows that Khiroda Sundari Dashya was only C.S. recorded tenant and before holding auction she sold her rayoti interest to Salimunnessa on 27.03.1953 who was not impleaded in the certificate procedure. That is, Khiroda had no right and title at the time of holding auction in suit property so the auction purchaser had not acquired any title because, at the time of holding auction the certificate debtor had no title in the property, in question. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that Salimunnessa had notice of the alleged charges brought by R.L. Acquired Government Estate either actual or constructive. It is to be relevant here to reiterating that in Title Suit No.221 of 1964, the learned Munsif observed that Khiroda and Lalit Mohon were the certificate debtors who already sold their interest to Salimunessa with the knowledge of the defendant No.1, that is, predecessor of the present plaintiffs. Lalit Mohan and Khiroda had no subsisting interest on the date of holding auction sale and it cannot be said that the defendant No.1 (predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs) acquired 7 annas interest by his purchase in the certificate sale. That judgment was upheld in Second Appeal No. 1095 of 1966. That finding is binding upon the plaintiffs. The effect of a sale under the PDR Act being to pass to the purchaser merely the right, title and interest of the person named as judgment debtor in the certificate, the purchaser acquires no right if the person appears to have i no interest in the property at the date of sale. That is, auction purchaser Ali Ahmed did not get any title under it. In Title Suit No.221 of 1964, Title Appeal No.50 1966 and Second Appeal No.1 095 of 1966, the respective Courts had taken notice of the same. But the plaintiffs did not meet up the issue raised and explain the consequences of the same. 

 26. Facts of the case has been fully stated by his lordship Mr. Justice Hasan Foez Siddique. I shall narrate only what is required in reference to my judgment. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 herein, as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 in the 2nd court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka for declaration of title to the land measuring an area of .568 ajutangsha of C.S. 394 Khatian No. 241 and C.S. plot No. 390/3940 with buildings and structures situate thereon (hereinafter mentioned as the suit property), for further declaration that the plaintiffs are not bound by the judgment and decree dated 15.11.1979 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 and also for further declaration that the kabala executed by the said Court on 27.02.1980 in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 was fraudulent, collusive, illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 29. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 (herein appellants) contested the suit by filing written statements admitting that Khiroda Shundari Daishya was the sixteen annas owner of the suit property. However, according to them, while Khiroda Shundari Daishya had been in possession of the suit property she sold the suit property to one Salimunnesa by a registered kabala being, No. 2042 dated 27.03.1953 and delivered possession thereof to her. Salimunnesa while had been in possession of the suit property, transferred her eight annas share to Rasheda Begum and the rest eight annas share to Mohammad Ilias on 15.06.1959. Mohammad Ilias by a registered deed of gift transferred his eight annas share to Rasheda Begum and delivered possession of the same to her. Thus, Rasheda Begum became 16(sixteen) annas owner of the suit property, Rasheda Begum had been in possession of the suit property by mutating her name. One Munjurul Hoq was a tenant in a portion of the suit property and he defaulted in paying monthly rents. So, Rasheda Begum filed Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka for realization of the arrear rents. Rasheda Begum also filed House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 for evicting her tenant Doctor Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed. But Ali Ahmed created two forged registered deeds of agreement on 16.11.1959 being deed No. 6904 and 6905 by forging the signatures of Rasheda Begum. On the same date, Manjurul Haque also procured two applications for compromise of the aforesaid money suit and the house rent control case in the name of Rasheda Begum and Khatumunnesa through forgery and under duress. In the compromise agreements Doctor Manjurul Haque claimed that he purchased 7(seven) annas share of the suit plot in the auction held on 18.06.1953. Whereupon, Rasheda Begum filed Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka praying for cancellation of said agreements dated 16.11.1959 and also for cancellation of the applications for compromise filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Control Case No. 598 of 1959. In the said suit these defendants claimed that Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash sold the suit property to Salimunnesa on 27.05.1954 and that Khatimunnesa, wife of Doctor Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed was a tenant under Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash and that after transfer of the suit property she become a tenant under Salimunnesa. Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 was decreed on 25.12.1965 in favour of Rasheda Begum declaring the registered agreements being Nos. 6904 and 6905 dated on 16.11.1959 as cancelled and ineffective. The trial Court further declared the compromise applications filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Control Case No. 598 of 1959 as cancelled. Doctor Manjurul Haque and Khatimunnesa than filed Title Appeal No. 50 of 1966 before the District Judge, Dhaka and the appeal was heard by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and was dismissed. Thereafter, Majurul Haque and his wife filed Second Appeal No. 1095 of 1966 before the High court Division but the said appeal was dismissed. Then the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title to the suit land and also for declaration that the plaintiffs are not bound by the judgment and decree dated 15.11.1979 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979. The plaintiff also filed Money Suit No.73 of 2000 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for realization of compensation of taka 28,71,900/-(twenty eight lacs seventy one thousand and nine hundred) along with interest @ of 15% till realization, and the Money Suit was transferred to the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and renumbered as Money Suit No. 2 of 2002. Both the suits were tried simultaneously and decreed in favour of plaintiffs, respondents herein. Thereafter, the defendants as appellants filed First Appeal No. 181 of 2004 before the High Court Division and the High Court Division by judgment dated 13 day of May, 2008 dismissed the appeals and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Whereupon, the present appellants filed CPLA. No. 1358-1359 of 2009 before this Division and this Division by order dated 13.05.2008 dismissed CPLA No. 1358 of 2009 arising out of Money Suit No. 02 of 2002 and LA No. 1359 of 2009 arising out of Title Suit No. 59 of 1994. Then the present appellants, who were defendants of the aforesaid suits filed Civil Review Petition No. 90 of 2010 before this Division. 

 "I. Whether the Gazette notification dated 2nd April 1956 No 4024 LR(sic No.4824 LR) and No.  4836 LR respectively under section 3 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (Act XXVIII of 1951) (hereinafter mentioned as the SA&T Act) as amended by E.P. Ordinance III of 1956, the rent receiving interest vested in the Government on 02.04. I 956 and exhibit-1 shows Khiroda Shundari Daishya held a Mirash Ijara  interest wider a private land lord and it conclusively proves that the certificate case No. 660 of 1952-53 issued by L.R. Government Acquired Estate are manufactured papers and exhibits-2 and 2(ka) are all also forged papers and the claim of title of the plaintiffs falls through. 

 II. Whether the finding that the certificate was filed by the Government for arrears of rent in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 while the exhibits 2 and 2(ka) show that certificate was filed by R.L. Government Acquired Estate against the provision of section 4 of Public Demand Recovery Act, 1913 (hereinafter referred to as the PDR Act) is a mistake apparent on the face of record and in the circumstances, judgment dated 06.05.2010 calls for review." 

 (1) Admittedly, Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohon Dash were original tenants of the suit property under a private zamindar (জমিদার) i.e. landlord Lakshmi Narayan and others as per Exhibit- 1 i.e. C.S. Khatian. (2) The root of plaintiffs case is that their predecessor in interest Ali Ahmed Dr. Monjurul Haque had purchased the suit property in auction from the R.L. Government Acquired Estates in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 through exhibit 2 and got possession thereof from the said estate through exhibit 2(ka). 

 (3) Gazette notification was published on 14 April, 1956 being notification No. LR 4826, LR 4836 acquiring the rent receiving interest by the Government and, as such, there was neither any scope of auction sell nor to deliver possession of the suit property by R.L. Government Acquired Estate in Auction by exhibits 2 and 2(ka). 

 (7) Lalit Mohan and Khiroda Shundari Daishya sold the suit property to Salimunnasa on 27.05.1954 and the Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 was filed by R.L. Government Acquired Estate under the PDR Act for arrear of rents, when the Government had no rent receiving interest. 

 (IV) the appellants suppressed the fact that their predecessor-in-interest Mohammad Joynal Abedin, father of appellant No. 1 had entered into an agreement to purchase the adjacent land to the suit property from one Piru Sardar @ Piru Miah under a registered agreement of sale executed on 24 July, 1964 and the said Joynal Abedin also purchased the same by registered conveyance deeds No. 3775 and 3776 for the year 1965 and that the adjacent land of the suit property was also auction purchased by Abdul Hug son of Lutfur Rahman from R.L. (Rup Lal) Government Acquired Estates in auction. So, the appellants cannot claim that the property could not have been sold in auction in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53. 

 (VI) the appellants' predecessor in interest Mohammad Ilyas had also taken lease in terms of registered deed of lease No. 3022 dated 16.06.1954 from Golam Mohammad who had purchased the same in Certificate Case No. 659 of 1952-53 of the Certificate Officer at 74, Bashanta Kumar Road, Dhaka and the Certificate Case was filed by the R.L. Government Acquired Estate and none else under the law. 

 (VII) the aforementioned registered deed of lease dated 16.06.1954 in the name of Mohammad Ilyas (predecessor in interest of the appellants) shows that the certificate case was filed by R.L. Government Acquired Estate, obviously under section 4 read with section 3(3) of the PDR Act. 

 (VIII)under the above facts and circumstances the appellants should not be allowed to dispute the statements in their own solemn deeds by the principle of 'estoppels by recitals in the deeds', and in that view of the matter, they should be debarred from disputing the similar facts with regard to the title of the respondents. 

 (IX) the plaintiff-respondents have not been able to search out Extra-ordinary Gazette Notification, dated Wednesday March 19, 1952 bearing No. 2906 L.R-28th February, 1952 by which Ruplal Wards Estate was acquired by the Government under section 3(1) of the SA&T Act). But from Extra-ordinary Gazette Notification dated February 12, 1954 bearing No. 1815 L.R. 6th February, 1954 it appears that reference has been given about acquisition of Rup Lal Wards Estate on 28.02.1952 under section 3(1) of the SA&T Act by Gazette Notification dated 19.03.1952. 

 (XI) R.L.(Rup Lal) Estate was owner of 7 annas share of Tauzi No. 61/1 (Part of Touzi No. 61) of Dhaka Collectorate and being Wards Estate it was being managed by the Government under the Court of Wards Act as prevalent. Therefore, by Notification No. 2906 L.R. dated 28.02.1952 as mentioned in the Gazette Notification No. 1815 L.R. dated 6111 February 1954, the Government got ownership of R.L. Estate. 

 (XII) the Government in order to realize the arrear rents of R.L.( Rup Lal) Court of Wards Estate from defaulter tenant Khiroda Shundari Daishya of C.S. Holding (Milts) No. 241 of Plot No. 390/3940 of the said Tauzi No. 61/1 filed Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 under section 62 read with section 139 and section 141 of SA&T Act against Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash and the suit property was sold in auction to Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque on 20.06.1953. Said auction was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and he got delivery of possession of the suit property measuring .568 ajutangsha on 20.01.1954 vide exhibits 2 and 2(ka). 

 (XIII)some other lands of Tauzi No. 61/1 of R.L. Estate were also sold in auction mentioning its 7 annas share of the said Tauzi on the same day (2.0.06.1953) vide Certificate Case No. 659 of 1952-53 and one Golam Mohammad purchased the land of Holding No. 246 in auction and got deliver y of possession on 28.04.1954. The said Golam Mohammad transferred the said land to Mohammad Iliyas, vide Deed of Lease in Perpetuity No. 3022 dated 16.06.1954 and the defendants eventually purchased the same. 

 (XIV) likewise some land of Holding No. 236 of R.L. Estate was also sold in Certificate Case No. 657 of 1952-53 of Tauzi No. 61/1 mentioning its 7 annas share and Golam Mohammad also purchased the same in auction. Thereafter, Golam Mohammad transferred the said plots to Mst. Habiban Nesa wife of Piru Sardar alias Piru Mia vide sale Deed No. 3827 dated 03.09.1954. The defendant - appellants subsequently purchased it. (XV) it is evident from exhibit 2 and 2(ka), deed of lease in perpetuity bein2 No. 1022 dated 16.06.1954 and sale deed No. 3827 and 03.09.1954 that R.L. Government Acquired Estate was the owner of 7 annas share of Tauzi No. 61/1, and it was the rent receiver. (XVI)Therefore, the Government being in management of R.L. Estate on 28.02.1952 legally sold the suit property to the plaintiffs' predecessor in interest in auction. All the alleged predecessor-in-interest of the defendants were never in possession of the suit property by their so called forged/fraudulent deeds of purchase at any time. Similarly, the defendants never dot possession of the suit property in due process of law at any time but they forcibly evicted the plaintiffs during pendency of the suit. 

 38. The ground taken in this appeal are that admittedly Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohon Das were tenants under private landlord and so, the sale certificate in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 issued by R.L. Government Acquired Estate and the writ of delivery of possession are manufactured documents as the rent receiving interest vested to the Government in the year, 1956 according to Gazette dated 02.04.1956. Thus, both exhibits 2 and 2(ka) are forged documents. 

 42. We are of the considered opinion that R.L. (Rup Lal) Court of Wards Estate was the owner of 7 annas share of Tauzi No. 61/1, which is a part of original Tauzi No. 61, of Sahar Dhaka of the Collectorate of Zilla-Dacca. It transpires from the C.S Khatian that it is written therein that Khiroda Shundari Daishya was in possession of No. 1, Atash Khana Lane of Mouza Sahar Dhaka of Khatian No. 241. This clearly shows that the words "Sahar Dhaka" as used in the auction sale certificate was the Mouza of the property sold in auction and the word “মৌজে আতস খানা” does not mean Mouza but it was the lane i.e. Mash Khana Lane. Further, from the deed of sale (Exbt-Ka) submitted by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 (appellants) it appears that the Police Station of the suit property has been stated therein as Kotwali at Present P.S.- Lalbag being premises No. 1, Atash Khana Lane, Dhaka. Thus it is evident that C.S. Khatian No. 241 was originally under P.S. Kotwali but subsequently it fell within P.S. Lalbag. Further, we searched the Gazette of establishment of Lalbag Police Station and finally it was found from the Culcutta Gazette, September 22, 19 45 that: 

 44. So, it appears that P.S. Lalbag was also correctly mentioned in the sale certificate. Therefore, R.L Estate was the owner of 7 annas share of the aforesaid Tauzi and .568 ajutangsha out of the said 7 annas was sold in auction from khatian No: 241 in favour of Ali Ahmed son of Late Munshi Nawab Jan on 20.06.1953. From the writ of delivery of possession (Exhibit 2(Ka) it appears that possession of the aforesaid land was delivered to Ali Ahmed. Relevant part of this document reads as under: 

 47. We have examined gazette notification dated February 12, 1954 submitted by Mr. M.I Farooqui, the relevant part of which is as under: `No. 1815 L.R.- 6th February 1954. — In exercise of the power conferred by sub-section (1) of section 46A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act No. XXVIII of 1951), the Governor is pleased to order that Compensation Assessment-rolls be prepared in respect of the properties of the rent-receivers mentioned in column 2 of the Schedule below which have been acquired under section 3 of the said Act by the notifications referred to in column 3 of the Schedule, on the basis of the returns, papers and documents furnished or taken possession of under sections 3A and 4 of that Act- 

 103. Babu Jagesh Chandra Das, son of Radhaballav Das, Babu Tarak Nath Das, son of Ramesh Chandra Das, of Farashganj, Dacca, (Wards, Ruplal Wards Estate, Dacca).	2906 L.R. dated 28.2.1952, under section 3(1). 

 48. Whereas the gazette notification dated 02.04.1956 as referred to by Mr. Quiyum reads as under: "No. 4836 L.R. — 2nd April 1956. — In exercise of the power conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act No. XXVIII of 1951), as amended by the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (East Bengal Ordinance No. III of 1956), it is hereby notified, for the information of all concerned, that the governor is leased to acquire, with effect from the 14th April 1956, all interests of all rent-receivers in their respective estates taluks, tenures, holdings and tenancies situated in the district of Dacca, including their interests in all sub-soil and rights to minerals in such estates, taluks, tenures, holdings and tenancies, except the interests and rights which have already been acquired by, and have already vested in, the Provincial Government under the provisions of the said Act." 

 49. Thus, Gazette notification dated 02 April, 1956 excludes the property of Rup Lal Acquired Estate as it was acquired earlier in 2906 LR dated 28.02.1952, published in Dhaka Gazette Extra-ordinary dated 19.03.1952, as apparent from Colum 03 of Gazette Notification dated February 12, 1954. 

 50. Therefore, it appears from the Dhaka Gazette Extra-ordinary published by the authority on February 12, 1954 that the Governor was pleased to order preparation of compensation of assessment roll of the properties which were acquired under section 3(1) of the SA&T Act by notification referred to in Colum 03. It further appears that Rup Lal Wards Estate, Dacca was acquired in 2906 L.R. dated 28.02.1952, under section 3(1) of the SA&T Act and it was notified in the Gazette on 19.03.1952. 

 51. In view of the above, it is evident that the entire R.L. (Rup Lal) Wards Estate, whether be it Tauzi No. 61 or 61/1, was under the management of the Government at the relevant time as a Wards Estate prior to 19.03.1952. Therefore, it appears that even prior to acquisition of rent receiving interest by the Government, it had the right to auction sale the suit property for arrear rents of Rup Lal Court of Wards Estate. 

 52. The defendant appellants claim the property through Salimunnesa as successor in interest. Salimunnesa's deed of purchase from Khiroda Shundari Daishya was on 27.03.1953. But it appears that the property was within the court of wards state and it was acquired prior to the sale by Khiroda Shundari Daishya in favour of Salimunnesa vide exhibit-Ka. 

 53. However, in the Gazette notification it is mentioned that the properties of Jogesh Chandra Das, son of Radhaballab Das, Babu Tarak Nath Das, son of Ramesh Chandra Das of Farashganj, Dacca were being managed by Wards, Rup Lal Wards Estate, Dacca. 

 54. None of the parties could explain about the Rup Lal Court of Wards Estate's ownership of the property but this Gazette Notification was never challenged by the defendants. Thus, the Government being in management of RL Wards Estate had lawfully auction sold the suit property of Wards Estate in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 and so, it cannot be said that the certificate of auction sale Exhibit- 2 is a forged document. 

 59. Moreover, admittedly the plaintiffs' predecessor in interest Doctor Monjurul Hoque @ Ali Ahmed had been in possession of the suit property by virtue of those documents as the defendants failed to prove monthly tenancy of Ali Ahmed or his wife under Khiroda Shundari Daishya or anyone else. Admittedly, the plaintiffs had also been in possession of the suit property, till they were dispossessed during the pendency of the suit. Possession follows title. 

 60. Further, even if for arguments sake it is presumed that Dr. Manjurul Huq @ Ali Ahmed or his wife Khalimunnessa was a monthly tenant under the Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Das or anyone else, in such case also, the plaintiffs cannot be evicted forcibly without following the process of eviction of a monthly tenant during pendency of the suit filed by the plaintiffs. It may be mentioned that though the defendants claim that Ali Ahmed/his wife was a tenant under Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Das but they failed to prove it by any iota of documentary evidence like monthly rent receipts, tenancy agreement, etc. 

 61. It may be mentioned that Exhibits 2 and 2 (ka) were marked as exhibits by the trial court without any objection from the defendants side. The defendants did not specifically mention with reasons that those documents arc forged documents in their written statement but their assertion was general in nature like the plaintiffs' assertion in the plaint that the defendants predecessors as well as the defendants deeds of purchases, bainapatra, etc. are all forged documents and paper transactions. The defendants also failed to prove that their predecessor-in-interests were ever in possession of the suit property by their so-called purchase. Thus, the registered deed of purchase from Khiroda Sundari Dasiya seems to be merely paper transaction as claimed by the plaintiffs. 

 62. Further, from the materials on rerecord it appears that some other lands of Tauzi Nos. 61 and 61/1 of R.L. Ward Estate were also sold in auction by mentioning its 7 annas share of the said Tauzi on the same day, i.e. on 20.06.1953 vide Certificate Case No. 659 of 1952-53 and one Golam Mohammad purchased land of Holding No. 246 in auction and got delivery of possession on 28.04.1954. The said Golam Mohammad transferred the said land to Mohammad Iliyas, vide Deed of Lease in Perpetuity No. 3022 dated 16.06.1954. Land of Holding .No. 236 of R.L. Estate was also sold in Certificate Case No. 657 of 1952-53 of Tauzi No. 61/1 mentioning its 7 annas share and Golam Mohammad also purchased the same in auction. Thereafter, Golam Mohammad transferred the said plots to Mst. Habiban Nesa wife of Piru Sardar alias Piru Mia, vide sale Deed No. 3827 dated 03.09.1954. So, it is evident that some other lands of Tauzi No. 61/1 were also sold in auction by R.L. Ward Estate, in certificate cases of 1952-53 of R.L. Acquired Estate. 

 "There is no allegation from defendants' side as to the non-genuineness of the documents of the plaintiff and that also no evidence was lead from the side of the defendant to show that the document placing reliance upon which the plaintiff is claiming the subject matter of the suit is not genuine, the question is in such a situation whether the Court is precluded from making decision in the background of the result of the scrutiny of document or documents of the plaintiff by the Court and thereupon refusing the relief sought by the plaintiff on the finding that the document relied upon by the plaintiff was not genuine. In our view even if there is no pleading from the side of the defendant alleging the non-genuineness of the document on the basis of which plaintiff is claiming the relief in the suit the Court has a duty in the interest of justice to scrutiny the document(s) relied upon by the plaintiff and if on such scrutiny the Court notices elements in the document that makes the same non-genuine, in the instant case as noticed by the appellate Court and stated hereinbefore, then in that situation the Court in spite of the absence of the pleading of the defendant as to the non-genuineness of the document of the plaintiff is quite competent to make its decision on the basis of the result obtained upon scrutiny of the document i.e. if on scrutiny document of the plaintiff is found not genuine the Court is competent to make its decision as against the plaintiff since his documents on which he based his claim not genuine." 

 70. In the instant case also Exbit-2 and 2(ka), i.e. auction sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession were marked as Exhibits on 05.01.2002 vide statement of P.W. 1, Murshed Kabir and no question was raised by the defendant-appellants before the trial court, the 1st appellate court and this Division in CPLA No. 1359 of 2009. Therefore, the principle laid down in the above noted case is applicable in the instant case. 

 73. We have already seen that in fact the Rup Lal Government Acquired Estate was the owner of 7 annas share of the Tauzi and out of it .568 ajutangsha of land was sold in auction. Moreover, the plaintiffs were admittedly in possession of the suit property. Therefore, if any one claims title to or ownership of the same or part of it, they shall have to file a suit for declaration of title, partition and possession. The defendants, under no circumstance were entitled to evict the plaintiffs from the suit property.
